intent: Adjusted geometry to improve lateral stability, line detection, and agility based on integrator feedback and race telemetry. Increased wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.14 to reduce steering oscillation and improve stability. Increased sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 to enhance line detection robustness, especially in curves. Reduced body_length from 0.18 to 0.16 to improve agility and reduce inertia during turns. These changes aim to help the controller maintain smoother line following with fewer line loss events and less oscillation.
rationale: Integrator feedback recommended increasing wheel_track to 0.14 for better lateral stability, increasing sensor_size to 0.016 for improved line detection, and reducing body_length to 0.16 for increased agility. The previous geometry had moderate steering oscillation (0.0748 on oval, 0.0669 on s-bend) and no line loss events, but the robot failed to complete the tracks, indicating room for improved stability and agility. Increasing wheel_track should reduce oscillations by providing better lateral stability. Increasing sensor_size should improve sensor sensitivity and robustness to noise, aiding line detection in curves. Reducing body_length should decrease inertia, allowing quicker turns and better responsiveness. These changes are expected to reduce steering oscillation, improve line following accuracy, and increase progress and completion rates. We request measurements on completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to verify these effects in the next iteration.
